Comments: No specific evidence found of CRVS integration with a national data exchange platform. Civil registration systems exist. Integration planned under broader digital government development.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The originally cited World Bank press release is generic funding news unrelated to CRVS and does not support the score. Direct evidence from Togo's National Identification Agency (ANID) states that, as of the e-ID rollout (2023-2025), the identity file is explicitly "not linked to the civil registry" to cross-check deaths, i.e. no automated CRVS feed exists. ANID's founding law tasks it with pursuing future interconnection between its Social Registry (RSPM) and other administrative databases, but this is a forward aim, not an implemented CRVS linkage. Recoded from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (Not integrated) on the strength of this explicit, dated statement; flagged for human review since the finding rests on a single (if authoritative) primary source discussing intended future development rather than an explicit "data exchange" assessment.
revised_comments: Togo's civil registration data is not currently linked to the national identification or data exchange systems. The National Identification Agency (ANID), which is developing the biometric e-ID and manages the Social Registry of Persons and Households, explicitly notes that identity records are not linked to the civil registry to cross-check deaths, meaning no real-time CRVS verification feed exists. ANID's legal mandate provides for future interconnection between its registries and other administrative databases, but this has not yet been implemented for civil registration data.

Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: No evidence found of electoral register integration with data exchange systems in Togo.

revised_year: Row was flagged for a light check as an unsourced Unknown, but the initial search surfaced clear, dated, corroborated evidence, so it was escalated to the full path. During the 2020 COVID-19 response, Togo's government cross-referenced the biometric voter registration (BVR) database — the country's most complete population database at the time — with mobile-phone data to verify identity and determine eligibility for the "Novissi" cash-transfer programme, in the explicit absence of a comprehensive social registry. This demonstrates genuine, if ad hoc, integration of electoral register data into a government service-delivery data flow. Recoded from 0 (Unknown) to 4 (Partially integrated). Flagged for human review because the clearest documented instance dates to 2020-2021 and it is unclear whether the electoral roll continues to be used this way now that ANID's own Social Registry (RSPM) has since been developed as the primary vehicle for beneficiary targeting.
status: Togo's biometric voter registration (BVR) database, last comprehensively updated in 2020 and holding records for over 3 million citizens, has been used to cross-reference and verify beneficiary identity and eligibility for the government's "Novissi" social-protection cash-transfer programme, in combination with mobile-phone data. This represents a documented instance of electoral register data being drawn on for identity verification and service-delivery targeting outside the electoral process itself.

status: Togo's National Employment Agency (ANPE), supported by UNDP, has built a digital labour-market monitoring platform that tracks job creation, layoffs, recruitment needs and graduate outflows in real time. As of December 2024, the agency was rolling out training on the platform to HR officers, IT staff and municipal officials across multiple regions (Lomé, Tsévié, Atakpamé, Kara, Sokodé). The platform remains a standalone employment-sector tool; no evidence confirms its integration with a wider government data exchange system.

Definition: Integration of court records, case management systems, correctional services data, legal aid information
Comments: No evidence found of justice/court system integration with data exchange in Togo.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown
revised_value_code: not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revised_year: Row was flagged for a light check as an unsourced Unknown; the initial search surfaced strong, recent, dated evidence, so it was escalated to the full path. On 2 July 2026 Togo's Ministry of Justice, working with the Agence Togo Digital (ATD), launched dematerialised payment and case-tracking for around 40 court services at the Tribunal de Grande Instance de Lomé via the national digital-services portal (new.service-public.gouv.tg), including mobile-money payment integration. This follows earlier justice-sector digitisation: the FORSETI commercial-court case-management platform (operational since 2019, handling online filing, automated judge assignment, and payments), and legislation establishing a national automated criminal record (casier judiciaire national automatisé). Together these show justice-system data and services genuinely connected to the national digital-government service layer, though so far only at one court, with plans to extend progressively to other jurisdictions and to recognise dematerialised acts in law. Recoded from 0 (Unknown) to 4 (Partially integrated).
status: Togo's justice sector is progressively connecting to the national digital government infrastructure. Since 2 July 2026, the Ministry of Justice and the Agence Togo Digital have enabled dematerialised payment and tracking of around 40 court services at the Tribunal de Grande Instance de Lomé through the national digital-services portal (new.service-public.gouv.tg), with payment via mobile money. This builds on the FORSETI platform, operational since 2019 for online filing, automated judge assignment and payment at the Lomé and Kara commercial courts, and on legislation establishing an automated national criminal record. Roll-out to other courts nationwide, and legal recognition of dematerialised judicial acts, is planned but not yet complete.

status: Togo's Road and Railway Transport Directorate (DTRF) has digitised driver-licensing and vehicle-matriculation processes, reported as roughly 85% complete, with an online portal (mit-dgt-dtrf.tg) for licence-test results and mobile-money payment options. The Togolese Revenue Office has also moved vehicle-registration requests onto its SYDONIA World customs platform. These remain standalone sectoral systems; there is no confirmed evidence that driver-licensing or traffic-offence data is exchanged with other government systems via a national data exchange platform.
